messages:
emily: Hey team — customer tenant `zen-prod-71` reporting a sudden p95/p99 regression starting ~10:05 UTC. They're seeing a ton of queued requests and increased 503/504s from the gateway. Customer says requests that used to finish in <200ms are now hitting 2–6s and occasionally 504.

raj: Can you paste the first failing request id + region so we can correlate? Any recent config changes for that tenant?

emily: Request id `req_0a1b2c3d`, region: us-west-2. No config changes from the customer side per CS notes. They did report a token rotation yesterday but that's unrelated? attaching minimal repro: hitting our /v1/generate endpoint with a 4k token prompt.

emily: repro snippet:
```
POST /v1/generate  HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood-inference.internal
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "open-llama-7b",
  "input": "<~4k token prompt>"
}
```

emily: response observed:
```
HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
x-rw-queue-length: 128
x-rw-admit-class: default
content-length: 0
```

nina: looking at traces now — I'm seeing a big pileup at the admission queue for nodes in the us-west-2 pool. p99 queue latency jumped from ~50ms to ~2.5s at 10:05. Concurrent inflight per-worker spiked; workers started returning 429-ish internal admission failures which the gateway turned into 504s.

nina: graph (short summary):
- cluster capacity steady
- tail latency on worker commit loop increases at 10:05
- KV cache hit rate drops (eviction churn) for the model shard serving this tenant

raj: @nina any signs of a deployment around 10:00? deploy-bot, did anything go out to us-west-2 at ~09:55–10:10?

deploy-bot: Canary rollout r-2026-03-15-198 deployed to us-west-2 at 09:58 UTC; 3/5 pods updated; no automated rollback triggered.

dario: That rollout touched an inference runtime change that altered kv-cache memory accounting + default concurrency_per_worker from 64 -> 96 for the new image. If workers accept more inflight they might thrash the KV cache and cause worse latency under tail loads.

dario: quick mitigation options:
- rollback the canary (safe but takes time)
- pin tenant to previous model variant (fast if pinning supported)
- reduce per-worker concurrency for the nodepool serving this tenant (surgical, immediate)
- enable early-reject admission policy (return 429 with Retry-After) for non-SLAs to shed load

nina: I can patch admission config to set per-worker concurrency from 96 -> 48 for the us-west-2 inference pool. That will reduce head-of-line blocking and let the KV cache stabilize. I'll also scale up worker count temporarily (+2 pods) to maintain throughput.

emily: Customer is unhappy and asking for ETA. Can we do the surgical change now and keep them updated?

raj: Yes. @nina please do the concurrency patch + +2 pods. Also add a temporary tenant-specific throttle: max_concurrency_for_tenant: 12 for `zen-prod-71` so their burst doesn't re-saturate queue.

nina: Applying patch now. Commands I'm running:
```
# reduce concurrency per worker in us-west-2 pool
kubectl -n inference patch cm admission-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"us-west-2.concurrency_per_worker":"48"}}'
# scale pool up 2 pods
kubectl -n inference scale deploy/worker-us-west-2 --replicas=7
# add tenant throttle
kubectl -n inference patch cm tenant-throttles --type merge -p '{"data":{"zen-prod-71":"12"}}'
```

nina: Patch applied and pods scaling. I'll watch queue length and p95.

~3 minutes later~

nina: Quick update — queue length dropped from 120 -> 18 over 90s, p95 fell from ~1.8s -> 220ms, p99 improving but still noisy (~900ms). KV cache eviction rate decreased.

dario: Good sign. I'd still recommend rolling back the canary because concurrency semantics were changed implicitly; we should treat that rollout as suspect. If we rollback we'll restore the previous concurrency default and avoid further surprises.

raj: Agreed. deploy-bot, can you initiate rollback for r-2026-03-15-198 in us-west-2 canary? Keep canary tags for diagnostics.

deploy-bot: Rollback started for canary r-2026-03-15-198 -> r-2026-03-14-142. Expected completion ~2m.

billing-bot: Note: tenant `zen-prod-71` has been near committed capacity for last 48h; they are also eligible for dedicated capacity upgrade. (informational)

emily: Customer update sent: we're investigating an internal runtime rollout that increased worker concurrency — we've temporarily reduced concurrency and added tenant throttle; tail latency improving. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline.

nina: Rollback completed. Post-rollback metrics: p95 steady ~180ms, p99 ~420ms. Queue length stable <20. I'll keep this thread open for 2 hours to watch regressions.

dario: Action items:
- runtime: add unit/regression test for concurrency config changes to avoid implicit defaults 
- infra: document safe canary throttle and a quick rollback playbook for admission regressions
- product/support: notify customers with high committed usage and suggest dedicated pool if consistent bursts occur

raj: Thanks everyone. Emily — please use this thread to paste the postmortem summary once we have root cause + timeline. Closing handoff to SRE/Runtime.

emily: Will do. Closing loop with customer now and will post follow-up. :white_check_mark:
